explanation: Match each pattern/text position with memoization. A starred token either consumes nothing or one matching character and stays available. A leading ^ restricts the start; a trailing $ requires the end. Otherwise try every substring start.
timeComplexity: O(p · (n + 1)) for pattern length p and text length n.
spaceComplexity: O(p · (n + 1)) memoization plus O(p + n) recursion stack.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Match(p,t) states whether the pattern suffix at p can match beginning at text position t under the end-anchor rule. A normal token must match one character; a starred token either takes zero repetitions or consumes one matching character and tries again. These cases are exhaustive. Memoization reuses identical suffix states, while start/end anchors constrain the allowed positions.
walkthrough: For regex "^ab*c$" and text "abbbc", the start anchor fixes position zero. Match a, let b* consume the three b characters, then match c at the text end. The end anchor succeeds, so return true.
edgeCases: An unanchored pattern may match an empty substring.
^ anchors only the beginning and a trailing $ anchors the end.
A starred token may consume zero characters.
Dot matches one character, not an arbitrary-length substring.
